title: Shifting patterns in clinical pharmacy interventions associated with the integration of a clinical decision support system: A retrospective pre–post study in Brazil
content:
by Tayná Letícia de Castro Santos, Patricia Carvalho Baruel Okumura, Christian Valle Morinaga, Pedro Kallas Curiati, Fábio de Cerqueira Lario

Introduction

Clinical decision support systems (CDSS) can enhance medication safety and optimize pharmacotherapy. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of implementing the Medi-Span CDSS, a rule-based artificial intelligence, on clinical pharmacy interventions in a tertiary care hospital.

Methods

This retrospective analysis compared clinical pharmacy interventions before and after CDSS integration with a computerized physician order entry (CPOE) system using data from electronic health records. Exploratory analysis included the associations between CDSS alerts and clinical outcomes.

Results

The proportion of hospitalizations with clinical pharmacy interventions increased after Medi-Span integration (13.4% vs. 11.2%, p < 0.01; adjusted OR=1.34, 95% CI: 1.26–1.41), with a shift toward therapeutic duplication (68.2% vs. 54.5%, p < 0.01) and a relative decrease in dose/posology interventions (44.6% vs. 54.8%, p < 0.01). Concurrently, unplanned intensive care unit admissions significantly decreased from 5.4% to 4.1% (p < 0.01), an association that remained significant in multivariate adjusted regression (OR=0.84, 95% CI: 0.77–0.91, p < 0.01; NNT = 118).

Conclusion

The implementation of the Medi-Span CDSS in our CPOE was associated with more clinical pharmacy interventions, as well as a shift in their pattern.
author: Tayná Letícia de Castro Santos
